builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout
summary: The method replaces manual analog opamp design iteration from specifications through layout and post-layout verification with a general-purpose LLM agent taught the gm/ID sizing methodology and a layout generator framework. It costs expert teaching effort, an open-source EDA stack (SKY130, gLayout), and designer-approved gates rather than GPU compute or model training. It can fail on process nodes or circuit topologies without characterized lookup tables, and agent-generated layouts still require designer sign-off and corner verification to remain trustworthy.
rationale: This is an EDA/agent application for analog circuit design, not an ML inference or training technique relevant to the reader's production adoption decisions.
technique: Expert-taught LLM agent for analog IC design

claims.statement: The method replaces manual analog opamp design iteration from specifications through layout and post-layout verification with a general-purpose LLM agent taught the gm/ID sizing methodology and a layout generator framework. It costs expert teaching effort, an open-source EDA stack (SKY130, gLayout), and designer-approved gates rather than GPU compute or model training. It can fail on process nodes or circuit topologies without characterized lookup tables, and agent-generated layouts still require designer sign-off and corner verification to remain trustworthy.
All six opamp layouts are DRC-clean and LVS-matched, with extracted netlists meeting every target at all 15 PVT corners (fun >= 53.7 MHz, PM >= 62.1 degrees, SR >= 27.9 V/us).
